name: Pale Saints
label: 4AD
lede: Ivo Watts-Russell heard a Leeds trio's demo, saw one London show and signed them. Pale Saints made three albums for 4AD, and the singer on the last one had started out fronting Lush.

eras.title: A demo that found its way to Ivo
eras.text: Singer-bassist Ian Masters, guitarist Graeme Naysmith and drummer Chris Cooper started in Leeds as a jangly indie-pop band in the mould of early Primal Scream. Within two years the songs had gone darker and noisier, Masters' choirboy voice was floating over the top, and 4AD had them.

years.h: Masters, Naysmith and Cooper start a band in Leeds
years.p: Masters sings and plays bass. The early sound is jangle, closer to early [[Primal Scream|55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a]] than to anything 4AD was putting out.

years.src: AllMusic: The Comforts of Madness · Wikipedia: Pale Saints
years.h: Ivo Watts-Russell catches one London gig and signs them
years.p: A demo, with "Sight of You" on it, brought the 4AD boss to the band's first London show. He signed Pale Saints after it, and according to AllMusic he signed the support act, [[Lush|697801d1-68b2-4413-a7e4-0ef507d21cc1]], too.
years.xp: AllMusic's Andy Kellman writes that Watts-Russell was particularly taken with "Sight of You" and caught a gig "without haste." Within months the trio were in the studio for 4AD.

years.h: Ashley Horner of Edsel Auctioneer passes through on guitar
years.p: Horner's stint in the band lasts part of 1989. He later became a film producer in Newcastle upon Tyne.

years.h: Barging Into the Presence of God makes No. 3 on the indie chart
years.p: Ivo sent the band in with [[Gil Norton|2270fb9d-0f39-4f6f-aba9-ef2bee2f3755]] and [[John Fryer|17375716-41de-49a9-8b9c-64c71bb14742]] for the three-song debut EP. It reached No. 3 on the UK Indie chart.
play: Barging Into the Presence of God

eras.title: 4AD's first record of the '90s
eras.text: The Comforts of Madness opened 4AD's decade and went Top 40. Then Meriel Barham, the singer Lush started with, joined on guitar and voice, and the band stopped being a three-piece of lads.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Comforts of Madness · Slicing Up Eyeballs: Comforts reissue
years.h: The Comforts of Madness reaches No. 40
years.p: Recorded at Blackwing in London with Fryer and Norton splitting the production, it was 4AD's first release of the 1990s. It includes a cover of Opal's "Fell from the Sun," written by Kendra Smith.
years.xp:
NME's Simon Williams heard "at least eight Great Pop Tunes" in it and put it at No. 45 on the paper's albums of 1990. A quarter century later Pitchfork ranked it No. 21 on its list of the 50 best shoegaze albums.

4AD reissued it, remastered and expanded with demos and the band's one John Peel session, on 17 January 2020.

years.h: MTV's 120 Minutes airs "Time Thief" and a chat
years.p: The band talk about the debut and why they covered Opal, and the "Time Thief" video gets its American airing.

q: It really changed the dynamic of the band completely.
years.src: Paste: Looking Back 30 Years · 4AD: Pale Saints · Wikipedia: Pale Saints
years.h: Lush's first singer joins the band
years.p: Meriel Barham, recommended by [[Miki Berenyi|00f7467f-462e-408c-8d57-ac10f33d8139]] of [[Lush|697801d1-68b2-4413-a7e4-0ef507d21cc1]], sings and plays guitar on the Half-Life EP and then joins for good. Masters told Paste it changed the band's dynamic completely.
years.xp: Masters said Barham's songs were immediately liked by everyone. Half-Life, produced by Chris Allison, came out in October 1990 and reached No. 86; the 12-inch carried a spoken-word bonus track, "Colour of the Sky."

years.h: A Nancy Sinatra cover gives them a chart single
years.p: "Kinky Love" leads the Flesh Balloon EP, the band's first session with producer [[Hugh Jones|d62cacb0-f4ef-4d77-9d7d-86232507ff1a]], and reaches No. 72.

years.cap: Masters, Naysmith, Cooper and Barham, c. 1991
years.h: On the road with the Pixies
years.p: 4AD puts its Leeds dream-pop band on tour with its loudest American one, the [[Pixies|b6b2bb8d-54a9-491f-9607-7b546023b433]].

eras.title: In Ribbons, and a singer who'd had enough
eras.text: In Ribbons was poppier, bigger and made across three studios, and the band now had two singers. Masters was already halfway out the door, and he left on a US tour the next year.

years.src: Paste: Looking Back 30 Years · Wikipedia: In Ribbons · 4AD: Pale Saints
years.h: In Ribbons arrives with a free brass-band single
years.p: Hugh Jones produced it at Monnow Valley, Palladium in Edinburgh and Blackwing between October 1991 and January 1992. First copies came with a 7-inch of the Tintwhistle Brass Band playing two Pale Saints songs.
years.xp:
The brass band recorded "A Thousand Stars Burst Open" and "A Revelation." Masters told Paste that Ivo had suggested Hugh Jones, that they argued over whether "Blue Flower" belonged on the LP, and that Jones would spend another 12 to 15 hours on a mix after everyone else was done.

"Blue Flower" ended up only on the US and Japanese editions. The album reached No. 61 in the UK and No. 10 on the indie chart; NME gave it 9 out of 10.

years.h: "Throwing Back the Apple" makes No. 93
years.p: The single from In Ribbons is the band's last chart entry.

years.big: "I knew I'd be miserable. I knew I'd hate it."
q: Ian became really fed up with the whole touring process.
years.src: Paste: Looking Back 30 Years · Snarl: Pale Saints interview · 4AD: Pale Saints
years.h: Ian Masters quits on a US tour
years.p: Masters, to Paste, on staying in a band he felt was heading somewhere more mainstream. He quit in 1993 over touring, and Canadian bassist [[Colleen Browne|17b2dab0-fffa-47c7-bdaa-e0c20a0a7e99]] took his place.
years.xp:
Masters told Paste he was "really on the point of leaving" even before In Ribbons was recorded. Barham's version, given in 1994, was that he left five or six weeks into a US tour, that touring had turned into repetition for him, and he was going in a different direction from the rest of the band.

He went straight into Spoonfed Hybrid with former A.C. Temple member Chris Trout, whose debut came out on 4AD's Guernica imprint that year.

eras.title: Barham at the front
eras.text: With Barham singing lead and Browne on bass, the Saints made one more album with Hugh Jones, toured Europe and the US, and recorded a Tom Waits song as their last act.

years.h: Fine Friend borrows from the Persian Rugs
years.p: The lead track of the EP is adapted from "Poison in the Airwaves," a 1981 song by Persian Rugs.

years.src: Snarl: Pale Saints interview · Wikipedia: Slow Buildings
years.h: On Slow Buildings, those footsteps are the producer's
years.p: The last album, made at Palladium and Parr Street with Hugh Jones and Mark Freegard, with Caroline Lavelle on cello. It reached No. 25 on the US CMJ chart.
years.xp:
Barham told an interviewer in 1994 that the footsteps heard on the album's 11-minute centrepiece belong to Hugh Jones: "He wears cowboy boots." The door slam is on there too.

Every song is credited to the four members, Barham, Browne, Cooper and Naysmith.

years.h: Barham's line-up tours Europe and America
years.p: The four-piece plays both continents in late autumn 1994. Barham, in 1994: the papers consider you old news after one album, so going abroad mattered.

years.h: The last recording is a Tom Waits song
years.p: "Jersey Girl" appears on Step Right Up: The Songs of Tom Waits. It's the final studio recording the band makes.

years.h: Barham leaves, and Pale Saints end the next year
years.p: Barham departs in September 1995 and the band is finished by 1996. Barham went on to record electronica as Kuchen for Karaoke Kalk.

eras.title: Reissues, and a guitarist gone
eras.text: 4AD brought the albums back in expanded editions. Masters, living in Japan since 2005, kept making music; Naysmith and Cooper kept playing together in Leeds until Naysmith's death in 2024.

years.h: Mrs. Dolphin hits vinyl, and "Sight of You" gets a video
years.p: The Japanese singles compilation gets its first vinyl pressing for Record Store Day. Masters makes a "Sight of You" video with Terako Terao, his partner in Big Beautiful Bluebottle.

years.h: In Ribbons comes back with its demos
years.p: 4AD's 30th-anniversary expanded edition includes the original demo of "Kinky Love."

years.src: Louder Than War: Graeme Naysmith · Wikipedia: Pale Saints
years.h: Graeme Naysmith dies
years.p: No cause was made public. After Pale Saints he and Cooper played together in Lorimer, the Terminals and Cyanide Pills, and Naysmith later formed the X-Rays Eyes.
